<description>
SQLite statements are C objects which can be long lived, so having them be initialized in a constructor, and cleanup everything in a destructor, makes the sqlite code cleaner and easier to read. This also lets us have the various functions needed to interact with sqlite statements be member functions.

This will be particularly useful in future work which makes use of more complicated SQL statements.
</description>

[2026-07-27] r:4790064267 review COMMENTED by pablomartin4btc (member):
ACK 1682818a7b19

Left some inline nits. Two broader observations I think worth noting:
- `GetNewPrefixCursor` bind failure is now a throw instead of `nullptr` -
Previously `GetNewPrefixCursor` returned `nullptr` when `BindBlobToStatement` failed, and callers handled that. Now the `SQLiteCursor` constructor throws `std::runtime_error` if either bind call fails, and no caller catches it — so it propagates up the stack. Also, since this PR introduces the behaviour change, wouldn't be natural to clean up the now-dead null-checks in `walletdb.cpp` (lines 193, 470, 523)?

- `sqlite3_prepare_v2` ignores trailing SQL (`pzTail`) -
The `SQLiteStatement` constructor passes `nullptr` as the `pzTail` out-parameter, so if `stmt_text` ever contained more than one statement (e.g. a stray semicolon — `"INSERT INTO main VALUES(?,?); DROP TABLE main"`), SQLite would silently prepare only the first and discard the rest (@Eunovo [raised](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33033/changes#r3645464121) it also).
